title: Deployment windshield and governance latency dashboard
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: As we scale multi-surface releases (runtime, console, API) there is recurring friction coordinating regional capacity, canary windows, and cross-team rollout ownership. Existing playbooks live in several places and are often interpreted differently by SRE, Platform, and PMs. This ticket creates a single "deployment windshield" product — a combined calendar + governance UI and a companion "latency governance" dashboard to make rollout risk explicit and automatable.

Goals: (1) Surface upcoming deploys with consumable risk signals (capacity headroom, KV cache warmup expectations, model-variant fallbacks). (2) Provide guardrails for scheduling (regional blackout windows, cohort slots, minimum preflight checks). (3) Generate machine-readable release slots (calendar-as-code) for the release conductor to consume. (4) Ship a latency governance dashboard that flags degradation relative to SLOs and correlates to active rollouts.

Scope: Product-spec + runbook + lightweight PoC dashboard panel and calendar-as-code schema. Implementation will integrate with release-conductor events, infra capacity API, and Console telemetry. Not in scope: full RBAC enforcement (follow-up).

Success metrics: 
- Reduce cross-team deploy scheduling conflicts by 80% (measured by conflicts detected vs last 3 quarters).
- Time-to-decision for go/no-go during week-of-launch reduced to <15 minutes for ops leads.
- Early detection: 90% of canary-related latency regressions surfaced within first 15m of rollout via the dashboard alerts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Draft product spec reviewed and approved by Eng, SRE, and Design.
- Calendar-as-code schema (OpenAPI-style) checked into repo and consumed by a minimal CI job that validates calendar slot YAMLs.
- Dashboard panel implemented in Console staging showing active rollouts, per-region headroom, and token-level cost delta.
- Release conductor can ingest slots via a small webhook/contract (PoC).

Stakeholders: 
- PM: Maya Chen (owner)
- Eng: Luca Romero (implementation lead), Priya Desai (runtime capacity), Omar Haddad (console telemetry)
- Design: Celia Park (UX for windshield)
- SRE: Tobi Nwosu (ops gating)

Planned deliverables: 
- Product spec (Confluence) + acceptance criteria
- calendar-as-code schema and validator (repo: github.com/redwood/release-calendar)
- Console dashboard panel (staging) with latency governance widgets
- Runbook for week-of-launch check-in sequence

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Over-automation could block legitimate emergency fixes. Mitigation: provide manual override and emergency lanes; require human confirmation for blocking actions.
- Risk: Data sparsity in new markets makes headroom signals noisy. Mitigation: use smoothed signals and confidence bands; label low-confidence slots.
- Risk: Cross-team buy-in delays adoption. Mitigation: early prototyping sessions with SRE and Platform and include a lightweight import path for current spreadsheets.

Next steps: 
1) Align spec with runtime and console leads (this week).
2) Design kickoff with Celia for windshield UI (next 5 working days).
3) Create calendar-as-code schema PR and CI validator (owner: Luca).
4) Wire a staging dashboard feed from Console telemetry (owner: Omar).

Notes: This approach intentionally separates decision surfaces (visibility + governance) from enforcement (RBAC, automatic throttles) to accelerate adoption. We expect enforcement features to be follow-ups once the windshield is producing high-quality signals.
